key_insight: ARGUS is an evidence-constrained agentic framework that separates deterministic genomic computation from LLM reasoning to avoid hallucinated variant interpretations and only reach conclusions supported by real biological evidence.
engineering_relevance: The paper shows how agent planning, verification, and uncertainty-aware tool use can make AI systems more trustworthy for high-stakes computational genomics and regulatory variant interpretation.
method: Wraps 458 DNABERT-based TF binding models inside a hypothesis-directed investigation loop
Uses an LLM planner to choose evidence sources while a deterministic verifier interprets each result
Routes queries through real ADASTRA, JASPAR, and ENCODE cCRE evidence with trajectories that can branch or abstain
evidence_signal: On rs6983267, the framework produced four TF-specific trajectories; FOXA1 was rescued by real ADASTRA data, KLF6 and RAD21 abstained after mixed or nonsignificant evidence, and all observations were based on real database queries rather than simulated results.
watch_item: The approach depends on the completeness and coverage of external evidence sources, so unresolved cases may still abstain when direct experimental support is missing.
paper_title: Unlocking the Regulatory Genome by ARGUS: An Evidence-Constrained Agentic Framework for Interpreting Single Nucleotide Variants
